Month: February 2019
This archive page from the International Cheese Federation website highlights various activities and news from February 2019. It includes details on food safety and packaging workshops, information about cheesemonger and judge certifications, member spotlights, updates on milk production and market trends, and advocacy efforts concerning inspection backlogs and federal agriculture data.

A slower milk week, and what it means for you 

 

Federal market reporting for this week shows milk production growth still barely above flat. Here’s what that quiet number actually means for members buying, not just making, cheese.

Cedar and the cave: notes from our packaging workshop 

 

A one-day workshop on cedar and wood packaging drew producers to Tandil this week, and it raised a question worth carrying home: does your wrap protect the rind, or fight it?

The inspection backlog, and what we’re asking on your behalf 

 

Routine facility inspections paused for over a month this winter and are only now catching up. Here’s what that backlog means for members and what our Food Safety Committee is pushing for.

The quiet lapse in your judge accreditation 

 

Competition Judge Accreditation lapses fast without active panel work. Here’s why it matters more in a crowded cheese case, and how the sensory pathway toward it actually runs.

Margins hold, and the cheese case doesn’t slow down 

 

A second federal safety-net payment landed this month, and specialty cheese kept outperforming the broader dairy case. Here’s what both numbers mean for members.

The numbers came back all at once 

 

Six weeks of missing federal agriculture data landed in a single release this morning. Here is what the federation is asking for on behalf of members who plan a year at a time.
